[[Religious sister (Catholic)|Sister]] '''Marion Beiter''' {{small|[[Order of St. Francis|OSF]]}} (August 23, 1907 –  October 11, 1982), born '''Dorothy Katharine Beiter''', was an American mathematician and educator. Her research focused on the area of [[cyclotomic polynomial]]s.{{r|ascent}}

Beiter was born in [[Buffalo, New York|Buffalo]] to Kathryn ({{nee|Kiel}}) and Edward Frederick Beiter, where she attended [[Buffalo Academy of the Sacred Heart|Sacred Heart Academy]].{{r|buf_cour_exp}} She entered the [[Sisters of St. Francis of Penance and Christian Charity]] in 1923, and professed her [[Religious vows|final vows]] in 1929.

She began her career in 1925 as a teacher in parochial and private schools, continuing in this capacity until 1952, when she was appointed chairwoman of the mathematics department of [[Daemen College|Rosary Hill College]]. She meanwhile graduated from [[Canisius College]] (1944) and [[St. Bonaventure University]] (1948), before obtaining a PhD from the [[Catholic University of America]] in 1960.{{r|whoswho}} In her work on cyclotomic polynomials and their coefficients she made a conjecture referred to as the [[Sister Beiter conjecture]].{{r|arxiv23}} Besides a sabbatical year at the [[University at Buffalo|State University of New York at Buffalo]] in 1971–1972, Beiter remained at Rosary Hill until her retirement in May 1977.{{r|ascent}}

Beiter died in 1982 of a series of [[stroke]]s.{{r|response}}
